name: Hyderabadi Biryani
description: Aromatic basmati rice cooked with spiced chicken and traditional Hyderabadi flavours.
steps: Wash the basmati rice thoroughly and soak it in water for 20 to 30 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chilli powder, turmeric, biryani masala, lemon juice and salt.
Add chopped mint leaves, coriander leaves and green chillies to the chicken. Mix everything thoroughly and allow the chicken to marinate for about 30 minutes.
Thinly slice the onions. Heat oil in a pan and fry the onions until they become golden brown. Remove them and keep them aside.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add salt and whole spices such as cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and bay leaf.
Add the soaked rice to the boiling water and cook until the rice is approximately 70 percent cooked. Drain the rice.
Place the marinated chicken in a heavy-bottomed pot and spread it evenly.
Add some fried onions, mint leaves and coriander leaves over the chicken.
Spread the partially cooked rice evenly over the chicken.
Top the rice with the remaining fried onions, mint and coriander. Saffron-infused milk can also be added if available.
Cover the pot tightly and cook on low heat until the chicken is fully cooked and the rice becomes fluffy.
Allow the biryani to rest for a few minutes before gently mixing the layers.
Serve hot with raita, salad or mirchi ka salan.

name: Sarva Pindi
description: A crispy traditional Telangana rice-flour pancake prepared with peanuts, sesame seeds and spices.
steps: Take rice flour in a large mixing bowl.
Add roasted peanuts, sesame seeds, chana dal, chopped green chillies, finely chopped onion, cumin seeds, curry leaves, red chilli powder and salt.
Mix all the ingredients thoroughly.
Gradually add water and knead the mixture into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Grease a flat pan with a little oil.
Take a portion of the dough and spread it directly on the pan using your fingers.
Make a few small holes in the dough and add a little oil into the holes.
Cover the pan and cook over medium-low heat.
Once the bottom becomes golden and crispy, carefully flip it.
Cook the other side until it becomes crisp.
Serve hot with chutney or curd.

name: Pachi Pulusu
description: A refreshing Telangana-style raw tamarind rasam made with onions, green chillies and spices.
steps: Soak tamarind in warm water for a few minutes.
Extract the tamarind pulp and remove the seeds and fibres.
Add water to the tamarind pulp until it reaches a thin consistency.
Finely chop the onion and green chillies.
Add the chopped onion and green chillies to the tamarind mixture.
Add salt, red chilli powder and a small amount of jaggery.
Lightly roast cumin seeds and sesame seeds and crush them.
Add the crushed spices to the tamarind mixture.
Mix everything thoroughly and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve as a refreshing accompaniment with rice.

name: Andhra Pulihora
description: Tangy and spicy Andhra-style tamarind rice prepared with peanuts and aromatic tempering.
steps: Cook the rice until the grains remain separate. Spread it on a wide plate and allow it to cool.
Soak tamarind in warm water and extract a thick pulp.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the peanuts until golden. Remove them and keep them aside.
In the same pan, add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add cumin seeds, chana dal and urad dal and fry until golden.
Add dried red chillies, green chillies and curry leaves.
Add turmeric and the tamarind pulp carefully.
Add salt and cook the tamarind mixture until it thickens and the raw smell disappears.
Allow the tamarind mixture to cool slightly.
Add the mixture to the cooled rice and gently combine.
Add the roasted peanuts and mix again.
Allow the pulihora to rest for some time so the flavours are absorbed before serving.

name: Gongura Pachadi
description: A famous Andhra chutney made from gongura leaves, red chillies and traditional spices.
steps: Remove the gongura leaves from their stems and wash them thoroughly.
Spread the leaves on a clean cloth and allow excess water to drain.
Heat a pan and dry roast the red chillies until aromatic. Remove and keep aside.
Add a little oil to the pan and cook the gongura leaves until they soften completely.
Allow the cooked leaves to cool.
Grind the roasted red chillies, garlic, cumin seeds and salt into a coarse mixture.
Add the cooked gongura leaves and grind until the desired chutney consistency is reached.
Prepare a tempering with oil and mustard seeds.
Pour the tempering over the chutney.
Mix well and serve with hot rice and ghee.

name: Gutti Vankaya
description: Baby brinjals stuffed with a rich roasted spice mixture and cooked in a traditional Andhra gravy.
steps: Wash the small brinjals and make two cuts from the bottom without separating the pieces.
Dry roast peanuts, sesame seeds and grated coconut separately until aromatic.
Allow the roasted ingredients to cool and grind them into a coarse powder.
Add red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder and salt to the mixture.
Add a little water and make a thick stuffing paste.
Carefully stuff each brinjal with the prepared spice mixture.
Heat oil in a wide pan and gently place the stuffed brinjals inside.
Cook them over low heat while turning occasionally.
Add ginger-garlic paste and remaining stuffing mixture.
Add a little water, cover the pan and cook until the brinjals become tender.
Remove the lid and cook until the gravy thickens and oil begins to separate.
Serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Sakinalu
description: A traditional Telangana festive snack made from rice flour and sesame seeds in a distinctive spiral shape.
steps: Wash and soak rice for several hours, then drain and dry it thoroughly if making fresh rice flour.
Place the rice flour in a mixing bowl.
Add sesame seeds, ajwain and salt.
Gradually add water and make a soft dough.
Take a small portion of dough and roll it into a thin rope.
Shape the rope into traditional circular spirals on a clean cloth or plate.
Allow the shaped sakinalu to dry slightly so they hold their shape.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Carefully place the sakinalu into the hot oil.
Fry until crisp and lightly golden.
Remove and drain on absorbent paper.
Allow them to cool completely before storing.

name: Jonna Rotte
description: A traditional Telangana flatbread made with jowar flour and served with curries and chutneys.
steps: Place jowar flour in a wide mixing bowl.
Add salt and mix well.
Gradually add warm water and bring the flour together into a soft dough.
Divide the dough into equal portions.
Take one portion and flatten it gently.
Using wet fingers, carefully spread the dough into a thin circular roti.
Heat a flat pan over medium heat.
Transfer the roti carefully onto the hot pan.
Cook one side until small bubbles appear.
Flip and cook the other side until lightly browned.
Cook directly over a flame briefly if desired for a roasted flavour.
Serve hot with dal, curry or chutney.

name: Mirchi Ka Salan
description: A rich Hyderabadi curry made with green chillies and a creamy peanut-sesame gravy.
steps: Wash the green chillies and make a slit along each chilli without cutting it completely.
Heat a little oil in a pan and lightly fry the chillies. Remove and keep aside.
Dry roast the peanuts, sesame seeds and coconut separately until fragrant.
Allow them to cool and grind them into a smooth paste with a little water.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds.
Add finely chopped onion and cook until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until its raw smell disappears.
Add turmeric and coriander powder.
Add the ground peanut-sesame paste and mix thoroughly.
Add tamarind pulp, salt and enough water to create a thick gravy.
Add the fried green chillies and cook on low heat until they become tender.
Simmer until the gravy thickens and oil begins to appear on the surface.
Serve hot with biryani or rice.

name: Bagara Rice
description: Fragrant Telangana rice cooked with whole spices, onions and fresh herbs.
steps: Wash and soak the basmati rice for about 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Add bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom and fry until aromatic.
Add sliced onions and green chillies.
Cook the onions until they become lightly golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell disappears.
Add mint and coriander leaves.
Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot.
Gently fry the rice for a couple of minutes.
Add the required amount of water and salt.
Bring the mixture to a boil.
Cover and cook on low heat until the rice is completely cooked.
Allow the rice to rest for a few minutes before serving.

name: Andhra Chicken Curry
description: A spicy and aromatic Andhra-style chicken curry prepared with traditional spices.
steps: Clean the chicken pieces thoroughly and drain excess water.
Heat oil in a heavy pan and add curry leaves.
Add finely sliced onions and cook until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell disappears.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they become soft.
Add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder.
Mix the spices well and cook briefly.
Add the chicken pieces and coat them thoroughly with the masala.
Cook the chicken for several minutes while stirring occasionally.
Add enough water to create the desired gravy.
Cover and cook on medium-low heat until the chicken is completely cooked.
Remove the lid and simmer until the gravy reaches the desired consistency.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Royyala Iguru
description: A spicy Andhra-style prawn preparation cooked with onions, tomatoes and aromatic spices.
steps: Clean the prawns thoroughly and remove the shell and vein if necessary.
Add turmeric and a little salt to the prawns and mix.
Heat oil in a pan and add curry leaves.
Add chopped onions and cook until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until aromatic.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add chilli powder, coriander powder and remaining turmeric.
Add the prawns and mix well with the masala.
Cook until the prawns become opaque and are properly cooked.
Continue cooking uncovered so excess moisture evaporates.
Simmer until the masala coats the prawns.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Garelu
description: Crispy Andhra-style urad dal vadas with a soft centre, traditionally served with chutney or sambar.
steps: Wash the urad dal thoroughly and soak it in enough water for several hours.
Drain the dal completely.
Grind the dal into a thick and fluffy batter using as little water as possible.
Transfer the batter to a bowl.
Add chopped green chillies, onion, cumin seeds, curry leaves and salt.
Mix the batter thoroughly.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Wet your hands lightly and take a small portion of batter.
Shape it into a round disc with a small hole in the centre.
Carefully place it into the hot oil.
Fry until golden and crisp on both sides.
Remove and drain excess oil.
Serve hot with chutney and sambar.

name: Bobbatlu
description: A traditional Andhra sweet flatbread filled with sweetened lentils and flavoured with cardamom.
steps: Wash the chana dal and cook it until soft but not excessively watery.
Drain any remaining water completely.
Add jaggery to the cooked dal and cook until the mixture thickens.
Add cardamom powder and mix well.
Allow the filling to cool and grind or mash it into a smooth mixture.
Prepare a soft dough using maida, a little salt, water and oil or ghee.
Allow the dough to rest for some time.
Divide both the dough and filling into equal portions.
Flatten a dough portion and place the filling in the centre.
Bring the edges together and seal the filling inside.
Gently flatten and roll it into a thin circular shape.
Cook on a hot pan with ghee until golden spots appear on both sides.
Serve warm.

name: Pootharekulu
description: A delicate traditional Andhra sweet made with thin rice sheets, powdered sugar and ghee.
steps: Prepare a thin batter using rice flour and water.
Heat a suitable wide cooking surface.
Apply a very thin layer of rice batter to create a delicate sheet.
Allow the sheet to cook briefly without browning it.
Carefully remove the thin rice sheet.
Repeat the process to prepare multiple sheets.
Place one sheet on a clean surface.
Brush it lightly with melted ghee.
Sprinkle powdered sugar and cardamom powder over the sheet.
Place another rice sheet on top.
Repeat the ghee and sugar layers according to the desired thickness.
Fold the layered sheets carefully.
Cut into suitable pieces and serve.

name: Daddojanam
description: Cooling South Indian curd rice prepared with rice, yogurt and a simple tempering.
steps: Cook the rice until soft and allow it to cool slightly.
Mash the rice gently.
Add curd and milk and mix until smooth.
Add salt and finely chopped ginger and green chilli.
Heat a small pan with oil.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add urad dal and fry until golden.
Add curry leaves and turn off the heat.
Pour the tempering over the curd rice.
Mix gently and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.

name: Kodi Kura
description: A traditional Andhra chicken curry with a rich blend of onions, spices and herbs.
steps: Clean the chicken and cut it into suitable pieces.
Heat oil in a heavy pan.
Add curry leaves and sliced onions.
Cook the onions until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until aromatic.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder.
Mix the spices thoroughly.
Add the chicken and coat each piece with the masala.
Cook for several minutes while stirring occasionally.
Add water according to the desired gravy consistency.
Cover and cook until the chicken is completely cooked.
Remove the lid and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Mamidikaya Pappu
description: A tangy Andhra dal made with raw mango, toor dal and a simple aromatic tempering.
steps: Wash the toor dal thoroughly.
Peel and cut the raw mango into small pieces.
Add dal, raw mango, green chillies and turmeric to a pressure cooker or suitable pot.
Add enough water and cook until the dal becomes soft.
Mash the cooked dal and mango together.
Add salt and adjust the consistency with water if needed.
Heat oil in a small pan for tempering.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add cumin seeds, dried red chillies, garlic and curry leaves.
Fry the tempering ingredients until aromatic.
Pour the tempering over the dal.
Mix well and serve hot with rice and ghee.

name: Pesara Pappu
description: A simple and nutritious Andhra-style moong dal preparation with a light tempering.
steps: Wash the moong dal thoroughly.
Add the dal, chopped tomato, green chillies and turmeric to a pot.
Add enough water and cook until the dal becomes soft.
Mash the cooked dal gently.
Add salt and adjust the consistency with water.
Heat oil in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add cumin seeds, garlic and curry leaves.
Cook the tempering until aromatic.
Pour the tempering over the dal.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve hot with rice.

name: Hyderabadi Haleem
description: A rich and hearty Hyderabadi dish made by slow-cooking meat, lentils, grains and aromatic spices.
steps: Wash the broken wheat and lentils thoroughly.
Soak the broken wheat and lentils separately for about 30 minutes.
Clean the mutton and cut it into suitable pieces.
Cook the mutton with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder, salt and enough water until tender.
Cook the soaked broken wheat and lentils separately until they become very soft.
Allow the cooked grains and lentils to cool slightly.
Mash or blend them until they form a thick, smooth mixture.
Shred or mash the cooked meat and combine it with the grain and lentil mixture.
Transfer everything to a heavy-bottomed pot.
Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring regularly so it does not stick to the bottom.
Add garam masala and adjust salt according to taste.
Continue slow cooking until the haleem becomes thick and creamy.
Prepare fried onions and keep them aside.
Garnish the haleem with fried onions, mint, coriander and a little ghee.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

name: Hyderabadi Khatti Dal
description: A tangy Hyderabadi dal prepared with toor dal, tomatoes, tamarind and aromatic tempering.
steps: Wash the toor dal thoroughly.
Add dal, chopped tomatoes, green chillies and turmeric to a pot or pressure cooker.
Add enough water and cook until the dal becomes soft.
Mash the cooked dal until smooth.
Soak tamarind in warm water and extract the pulp.
Add the tamarind pulp, red chilli powder and salt to the dal.
Add water to adjust the consistency and simmer for several minutes.
Heat oil in a small pan for tempering.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add cumin seeds, dried red chillies, garlic and curry leaves.
Cook until the tempering becomes aromatic.
Pour the tempering over the dal.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice.

name: Hyderabadi Mirchi Bajji
description: Crispy fried green chillies coated in spiced gram flour batter, a popular Telangana-style snack.
steps: Wash the green chillies and make a slit along each chilli.
Remove some of the seeds if you prefer a milder flavour.
In a bowl, combine gram flour, rice flour, chilli powder, cumin powder, baking soda and salt.
Gradually add water and prepare a thick, smooth batter.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Dip each green chilli completely into the batter.
Carefully place the coated chillies into the hot oil.
Fry until the outer coating becomes crisp and golden.
Remove and drain on absorbent paper.
Serve hot with chutney or tea.

name: Telangana Chicken Fry
description: A spicy Telangana-style chicken preparation cooked with onions, curry leaves and aromatic spices.
steps: Clean the chicken pieces and drain excess water.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt to the chicken.
Mix thoroughly and allow it to rest for about 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a wide pan.
Add curry leaves and sliced onions.
Cook the onions until lightly golden.
Add the marinated chicken and mix well.
Cover and cook until the chicken releases its moisture and becomes tender.
Add coriander powder and cumin powder.
Add sliced green chillies and continue cooking uncovered.
Cook until the excess moisture evaporates and the masala coats the chicken.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Boti Curry
description: A traditional spicy Telangana meat preparation cooked with onions and aromatic spices.
steps: Clean the meat pieces thoroughly.
Heat oil in a heavy pan.
Add curry leaves and sliced onions.
Cook until the onions become golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until aromatic.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder.
Add the meat pieces and mix thoroughly with the masala.
Add water and cook until the meat becomes tender.
Continue simmering until the gravy reaches the desired consistency.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Kachchi Aam Dal
description: A tangy Andhra dal prepared with raw mango and lentils, especially popular during mango season.
steps: Wash the toor dal thoroughly.
Peel the raw mango and cut it into small pieces.
Add dal, mango pieces, green chillies and turmeric to a cooking pot.
Add enough water and cook until the dal becomes soft.
Mash the cooked dal and mango together.
Add salt and adjust the consistency with water.
Heat oil in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add cumin seeds, dried red chillies, garlic and curry leaves.
Cook the tempering until aromatic.
Pour the tempering over the dal.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with hot rice.

name: Andhra Tomato Pappu
description: A comforting Andhra-style dal made with tomatoes, toor dal and a fragrant tempering.
steps: Wash the toor dal thoroughly.
Add dal, chopped tomatoes, green chillies and turmeric to a pot.
Add enough water and cook until the dal becomes soft.
Mash the cooked dal gently.
Add red chilli powder and salt.
Adjust the consistency with water and simmer for a few minutes.
Heat oil in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add cumin seeds, garlic, dried red chillies and curry leaves.
Cook until aromatic.
Pour the tempering over the dal.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice.

name: Andhra Bendakaya Fry
description: A simple Andhra-style okra fry seasoned with spices and cooked until lightly crisp.
steps: Wash the okra thoroughly and dry it completely.
Cut the okra into thin pieces.
Heat oil in a wide pan.
Add curry leaves and sliced green chillies.
Add chopped onion and cook until lightly golden.
Add the chopped okra.
Cook uncovered while stirring occasionally.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder.
Add salt and mix well.
Continue cooking until the okra becomes tender and lightly crisp.
Serve hot with rice and dal.

name: Andhra Avakaya
description: A famous Andhra raw mango pickle made with mustard, chilli powder, salt and oil.
steps: Wash the raw mangoes and dry them completely.
Cut the mangoes into medium-sized pieces while keeping the skin on.
Place the mango pieces in a completely dry mixing bowl.
Add mustard powder, chilli powder, salt and turmeric.
Add garlic cloves and mix carefully.
Gradually add sesame oil and combine everything thoroughly.
Transfer the mixture to a clean, completely dry jar.
Ensure the mango pieces are well coated with the spice mixture.
Allow the pickle to rest so the flavours develop.
Store in a clean, dry container and use a dry spoon when serving.

name: Andhra Pesarattu
description: A nutritious Andhra breakfast made from soaked green gram and spices, cooked like a thin savoury crepe.
steps: Wash the green gram thoroughly and soak it in water for several hours.
Drain the soaked green gram.
Add green gram, green chillies, ginger, cumin seeds and salt to a blender.
Add enough water and blend into a smooth but slightly coarse batter.
Transfer the batter to a bowl and adjust the consistency with water.
Heat a flat pan over medium heat.
Pour a ladleful of batter onto the pan.
Spread it into a thin circular shape.
Sprinkle chopped onion and coriander leaves over the top.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges.
Cook until the bottom becomes golden and the edges crisp.
Flip if desired and cook briefly on the other side.
Serve hot with ginger chutney.

name: Ariselu
description: A traditional festive sweet made with rice flour and jaggery, popular in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
steps: Wash the rice thoroughly and soak it in water for several hours.
Drain the rice and allow excess water to leave without drying it completely.
Grind the rice into a fine flour.
Sieve the flour to remove coarse particles.
Melt jaggery with a small amount of water in a pan.
Cook until the jaggery syrup reaches a thick consistency suitable for binding the flour.
Add sesame seeds and cardamom powder.
Gradually add rice flour and mix to form a soft dough.
Allow the dough to rest for some time.
Take a small portion and flatten it into a thin disc.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Carefully fry the discs until they become lightly golden.
Remove and gently press to drain excess oil.
Allow them to cool before serving.

name: Hyderabadi Bagara Baingan
description: A classic Hyderabadi curry made with tender baby brinjals cooked in a rich peanut, sesame and tamarind gravy.
steps: Wash the brinjals and make two cuts from the bottom without separating them completely.
Dry roast the peanuts, sesame seeds and coconut separately until aromatic.
Allow the roasted ingredients to cool and grind them into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a wide pan and lightly fry the brinjals. Remove and keep aside.
Add chopped onion to the same pan and cook until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until aromatic.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder.
Add the ground peanut-sesame paste and mix well.
Add tamarind pulp, salt and enough water to make a thick gravy.
Add the fried brinjals and curry leaves.
Cover and cook on low heat until the brinjals become tender.
Simmer uncovered until the gravy thickens.
Serve hot with rice or biryani.

name: Telangana Kodi Pulusu
description: A tangy and spicy Telangana chicken curry prepared with tamarind, onions and traditional spices.
steps: Clean the chicken pieces thoroughly.
Soak tamarind in warm water and extract the pulp.
Heat oil in a heavy pan.
Add curry leaves and sliced onions.
Cook until the onions become golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until aromatic.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder.
Add chicken pieces and mix thoroughly.
Cook for several minutes until the chicken is coated with the masala.
Add tamarind pulp, salt and enough water.
Cover and cook until the chicken is completely cooked.
Simmer uncovered until the gravy reaches the desired consistency.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice.

name: Kodi Vepudu
description: A spicy Andhra chicken fry cooked with onions, curry leaves and aromatic spices.
steps: Clean the chicken and drain excess water.
Combine chicken with turmeric, chilli powder, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt.
Allow the chicken to marinate for about 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a wide pan.
Add curry leaves and sliced onions.
Cook until the onions become lightly golden.
Add the marinated chicken and mix well.
Cover and cook until the chicken becomes tender.
Add coriander powder and cumin powder.
Add sliced green chillies.
Cook uncovered until excess moisture evaporates.
Continue cooking until the masala coats the chicken.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Gongura Chicken
description: A popular Andhra chicken curry combining tender chicken with the distinctive tangy flavour of gongura leaves.
steps: Remove the gongura leaves from their stems and wash them thoroughly.
Heat a little oil in a pan and cook the gongura leaves until they soften.
Allow the leaves to cool and grind them into a coarse paste.
Heat oil in a heavy pan.
Add curry leaves and sliced onions.
Cook until the onions become golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until aromatic.
Add turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder.
Add the chicken pieces and mix thoroughly.
Cover and cook until the chicken becomes tender.
Add the gongura paste and sliced green chillies.
Mix well and simmer until the flavours combine.
Adjust salt and cook until the gravy reaches the desired consistency.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice.

name: Andhra Egg Curry
description: A spicy Andhra-style egg curry prepared with boiled eggs, onions, tomatoes and traditional spices.
steps: Boil the eggs until completely cooked.
Cool the eggs, remove their shells and make a few shallow cuts on them.
Heat a little oil and lightly fry the eggs with a pinch of turmeric and salt.
Remove the eggs and keep them aside.
Heat oil in the same pan.
Add curry leaves, chopped onions and green chillies.
Cook until the onions become golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until aromatic.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder.
Add water and salt to create the gravy.
Add the fried eggs and simmer for several minutes.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with rice or roti.

name: Andhra Daddojanam with Pomegranate
description: A refreshing Andhra-style curd rice enhanced with pomegranate, herbs and a simple tempering.
steps: Allow the cooked rice to cool slightly.
Mash the rice gently.
Add curd and milk and mix until smooth.
Add salt, chopped ginger and green chilli.
Heat oil in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add urad dal and cook until golden.
Add curry leaves and turn off the heat.
Pour the tempering over the curd rice.
Add pomegranate seeds and chopped coriander leaves.
Mix gently and serve chilled or at room temperature.

name: Andhra Masala Vada
description: Crispy Andhra-style masala vadas made with soaked chana dal, onions, herbs and spices.
steps: Wash the chana dal and soak it for several hours.
Drain the dal thoroughly.
Grind most of the dal into a coarse mixture while keeping some whole for texture.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl.
Add chopped onion, green chillies, ginger, cumin, fennel seeds, curry leaves and coriander.
Add chilli powder and salt.
Mix everything thoroughly.
Take a small portion and flatten it into a round disc.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Carefully place the vadas into the hot oil.
Fry until crisp and golden on both sides.
Remove and drain excess oil.
Serve hot with chutney.

name: Poornalu
description: A traditional Andhra festive sweet made with a sweet lentil filling coated in rice and urad dal batter.
steps: Wash and soak the rice and urad dal separately for several hours.
Cook the chana dal until soft and drain excess water.
Add jaggery to the cooked dal and cook until the mixture becomes thick.
Add cardamom powder and mix well.
Allow the filling to cool and shape it into small balls.
Grind the soaked rice and urad dal into a smooth batter.
Add a little salt and adjust the batter to a thick coating consistency.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Dip each sweet filling ball completely into the batter.
Carefully place it into the hot oil.
Fry until golden and evenly cooked.
Remove and drain excess oil.
Serve warm.

name: Gongura Rice
description: Tangy Andhra-style rice prepared with gongura leaves, spices and a fragrant tempering.
steps: Wash the gongura leaves thoroughly and remove excess water.
Heat a little oil in a pan and cook the gongura leaves until soft.
Allow them to cool.
Roast the dried red chillies and garlic lightly.
Grind the gongura leaves, red chillies and garlic into a coarse paste.
Heat oil in a wide pan.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add cumin seeds, urad dal and chana dal.
Add curry leaves and turmeric.
Add the gongura paste and cook for a few minutes.
Add salt and mix well.
Add the cooled cooked rice and gently combine.
Cook on low heat for a few minutes so the flavours blend.
Serve warm.

name: Kakinada Kaja
description: A famous Andhra sweet made from layered flour dough, deep-fried and soaked in sugar syrup.
steps: Place maida in a mixing bowl.
Add a little ghee and mix well.
Gradually add water and prepare a soft dough.
Cover and allow the dough to rest.
Prepare a thick sugar syrup with sugar and water.
Add cardamom powder to the syrup and keep it warm.
Divide the dough into small portions.
Roll each portion into a thin sheet.
Brush the sheet lightly with ghee and sprinkle rice flour.
Roll the sheet tightly and cut it into small pieces.
Flatten each piece gently.
Heat oil over medium heat.
Fry the pieces slowly until crisp and golden.
Drain excess oil.
Place the fried kaja in warm sugar syrup for a few minutes.
Remove and allow the syrup coating to set before serving.

name: Andhra Gongura Pappu
description: A tangy Andhra dal combining toor dal with gongura leaves and a traditional garlic tempering.
steps: Wash the toor dal thoroughly.
Wash the gongura leaves and remove them from their stems.
Add dal, gongura leaves, green chillies and turmeric to a pot.
Add enough water and cook until the dal becomes soft.
Mash the cooked dal and gongura together.
Add red chilli powder and salt.
Adjust the consistency with water and simmer for a few minutes.
Heat oil in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add cumin seeds, garlic, dried red chillies and curry leaves.
Cook until the tempering becomes aromatic.
Pour the tempering over the dal.
Mix well and serve hot with rice.

name: Andhra Gutti Dondakaya
description: Tender ivy gourds stuffed with a roasted peanut and spice mixture and cooked in Andhra style.
steps: Wash the ivy gourds thoroughly.
Make two crosswise cuts in each ivy gourd without separating the pieces.
Dry roast peanuts, sesame seeds and coconut until aromatic.
Allow them to cool and grind into a coarse powder.
Add chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric and salt.
Mix with a little water to form a thick stuffing.
Carefully stuff each ivy gourd with the prepared mixture.
Heat oil in a wide pan.
Add curry leaves and sliced onion.
Place the stuffed ivy gourds into the pan.
Cover and cook over low heat.
Turn them gently from time to time.
Cook until the ivy gourds become tender and the stuffing is lightly roasted.
Serve hot with rice.

name: Andhra Gongura Pachadi with Garlic
description: A bold Andhra-style gongura chutney prepared with red chillies, garlic and traditional tempering.
steps: Wash the gongura leaves thoroughly and remove the stems.
Heat a little oil in a pan.
Add the gongura leaves and cook until they soften.
Remove and allow them to cool.
Dry roast the dried red chillies and cumin seeds.
Allow the roasted ingredients to cool.
Grind the red chillies, cumin seeds, garlic and salt into a coarse paste.
Add the cooked gongura leaves and grind to the desired consistency.
Heat oil in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add urad dal and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over the chutney.
Mix well and serve with hot rice.

name: Andhra Chicken Biryani
description: A flavorful Andhra-style chicken biryani prepared with fragrant rice, spices, herbs and marinated chicken.
steps: Wash and soak the basmati rice for about 20 to 30 minutes.
Combine chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, turmeric, biryani masala, lemon juice and salt.
Add chopped mint, coriander and green chillies.
Mix well and allow the chicken to marinate.
Slice the onions and fry them until golden. Keep them aside.
Boil water with salt and whole spices.
Add the soaked rice and cook until it is about 70 percent done.
Drain the rice.
Cook the marinated chicken in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Spread the partially cooked rice over the chicken.
Top with fried onions, mint and coriander.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat until the chicken and rice are completely cooked.
Allow the biryani to rest for a few minutes.
Gently mix the layers and serve hot.

name: Royyala Vepudu
description: A spicy Andhra prawn fry cooked with onions, curry leaves and aromatic chilli spices.
steps: Clean the prawns thoroughly and drain excess water.
Mix prawns with turmeric, chilli powder, lemon juice and salt.
Allow them to rest for about 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a wide pan.
Add curry leaves and sliced onions.
Cook until the onions become golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until aromatic.
Add the marinated prawns and mix well.
Add coriander powder and cumin powder.
Cook until the prawns are properly cooked.
Continue cooking uncovered so excess moisture evaporates.
Add sliced green chillies.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Ulavacharu
description: A traditional Andhra horse gram preparation with a deep, earthy flavour and tangy finish.
steps: Wash the horse gram thoroughly.
Cook the horse gram in plenty of water until it becomes soft.
Strain and reserve the cooking liquid.
Mash some of the cooked horse gram and set aside.
Soak tamarind and extract its pulp.
Combine the reserved horse gram liquid with tamarind pulp.
Add tomatoes, green chillies, turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
Simmer the mixture until it reduces and develops a rich flavour.
Add some mashed horse gram to thicken the preparation.
Heat oil in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, dried red chillies, garlic and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering into the ulavacharu.
Simmer briefly and serve hot with rice.

name: Andhra Peanut Chutney
description: A creamy and spicy Andhra peanut chutney made with roasted peanuts, chillies and garlic.
steps: Dry roast the peanuts until aromatic.
Allow them to cool and remove the skins if desired.
Roast the dried red chillies and cumin seeds lightly.
Add peanuts, chillies, garlic, tamarind and salt to a blender.
Add a little water and grind into a smooth or slightly coarse chutney.
Adjust the consistency with additional water.
Heat a little oil in a small pan.
Prepare a simple tempering if desired.
Pour the tempering over the chutney.
Mix well and serve with dosa, idli or rice.

name: Andhra Pesara Punukulu
description: Crispy Andhra snack made from green gram batter, spices and herbs, deep-fried until golden.
steps: Wash the green gram and soak it for several hours.
Drain the soaked green gram.
Grind it into a thick, slightly coarse batter with ginger and green chillies.
Transfer the batter to a bowl.
Add chopped onion, cumin seeds, curry leaves and coriander leaves.
Add chilli powder and salt.
Mix everything thoroughly.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Take small portions of batter and carefully drop them into the oil.
Fry until golden and crisp.
Remove and drain excess oil.
Serve hot with chutney.

name: Nimmakaya Pulihora
description: A bright and tangy Andhra lemon rice prepared with peanuts, green chillies and a traditional tempering.
steps: Cook the rice and spread it on a wide plate to cool.
Squeeze the lemons and keep the juice aside.
Heat oil in a pan.
Fry the peanuts until lightly golden and keep them aside.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add cumin seeds, chana dal and urad dal.
Add dried red chillies, green chillies and curry leaves.
Add turmeric and switch off the heat.
Allow the tempering to cool slightly.
Add lemon juice and salt to the tempering.
Pour the mixture over the cooled rice.
Add the roasted peanuts.
Mix gently and allow the rice to rest before serving.

name: Bandar Laddu
description: A traditional Andhra sweet made from gram flour, sugar and ghee, associated with the coastal town of Machilipatnam.
steps: Prepare a smooth gram flour batter using gram flour and water.
Heat oil in a deep pan.
Prepare small boondi by passing the batter through a suitable perforated ladle into the hot oil.
Fry the boondi lightly and remove from the oil.
Prepare a sugar syrup by heating sugar with a small amount of water.
Cook until the syrup reaches a suitable sticky consistency.
Add the prepared boondi to the warm syrup.
Add cardamom powder, cashews and raisins.
Add melted ghee and mix thoroughly.
Allow the mixture to cool until it is comfortable to handle.
Take small portions and shape them into round laddus.
Allow the laddus to cool completely before serving.

Pour the tempering over the dal.
Mix well and serve hot with rice.

name: Bisi Bele Bath
description: A comforting Karnataka dish made with rice, lentils, vegetables, tamarind and aromatic bisi bele bath spices.
steps: Wash the rice and toor dal thoroughly.
Cook the rice and dal together until soft.
Cut the vegetables into small pieces.
Cook the vegetables separately until tender.
Soak the tamarind and extract the pulp.
Heat oil in a large pan and add mustard seeds.
Add cumin seeds, dried red chillies and curry leaves.
Add chopped onion and cook until soft.
Add chopped tomato and cook until soft.
Add turmeric and bisi bele bath masala.
Add the cooked vegetables and tamarind pulp.
Add salt and enough water and simmer for a few minutes.
Add the cooked rice and dal and mix gently.
Cook on low heat until everything combines into a thick consistency.
Add ghee if desired and serve hot.

name: Mysore Masala Dosa
description: A crisp Karnataka-style dosa spread with spicy red chutney and filled with seasoned potato masala.
steps: Boil the potatoes until tender and peel them.
Mash the potatoes into small pieces.
Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds.
Add urad dal and curry leaves.
Add sliced onion and green chillies and cook until soft.
Add turmeric and salt.
Add the mashed potatoes and mix well.
Garnish with coriander leaves and keep the masala aside.
Heat a dosa pan and spread a thin layer of dosa batter.
Cook until the dosa becomes crisp.
Spread a thin layer of red chutney over the dosa.
Place some potato masala in the centre.
Fold the dosa and serve hot with chutney and sambar.

name: Ragi Mudde
description: A traditional Karnataka staple made by cooking ragi flour with water and shaping it into soft balls.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Add salt and a little ghee.
Reserve a small amount of water and gradually add ragi flour to the remaining boiling water.
Do not mix immediately; allow the flour to cook briefly.
Using a wooden spoon, mix vigorously until the flour combines with the water.
Add the reserved water if the mixture becomes too thick.
Cook on low heat until the mixture becomes smooth.
Turn off the heat and allow it to cool slightly.
Wet your hands carefully and shape the mixture into smooth round balls.
Serve warm with sambar, saaru or curry.

name: Neer Dosa
description: A thin and soft coastal Karnataka rice crepe made from a simple rice batter.
steps: Wash the rice thoroughly and soak it for several hours.
Drain the rice.
Grind the rice with enough water to make a very smooth batter.
Add salt and mix well.
Add more water until the batter becomes very thin and flowing.
Heat a dosa pan over medium heat.
Lightly grease the pan.
Pour the batter quickly around the pan to form a thin dosa.
Cover and cook until the dosa is set.
Do not necessarily flip the dosa.
Fold it gently and remove from the pan.
Repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve hot with chutney or vegetable curry.

name: Akki Roti
description: A traditional Karnataka rice-flour flatbread mixed with vegetables, herbs and spices.
steps: Place rice flour in a large mixing bowl.
Add finely chopped onion, grated carrot, green chillies and coconut.
Add coriander leaves, curry leaves, cumin seeds and salt.
Mix everything thoroughly.
Gradually add water and prepare a soft dough.
Take a portion of dough and spread it thinly on a greased pan using wet fingers.
Make a few small holes in the dough.
Add a little oil around the edges and into the holes.
Place the pan over medium heat.
Cover and cook until the bottom becomes crisp.
Carefully flip and cook the other side.
Serve hot with chutney or curry.

name: Maddur Vada
description: A crispy Karnataka snack made with rice flour, semolina, onion and spices.
steps: Combine rice flour, semolina and maida in a mixing bowl.
Add finely chopped onion and green chillies.
Add cumin seeds, curry leaves, coriander leaves, chilli powder and salt.
Mix all the ingredients thoroughly.
Gradually add water and prepare a firm dough.
Take a small portion and flatten it into a thin round disc.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Carefully place the vada into the hot oil.
Fry until crisp and golden on both sides.
Remove and drain excess oil.
Serve warm with coconut chutney.

name: Vangi Bath
description: A flavorful Karnataka brinjal rice prepared with roasted spices and cooked rice.
steps: Cook the rice and allow it to cool.
Cut the brinjals into thin pieces.
Heat oil in a wide pan.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add urad dal, curry leaves and peanuts.
Add sliced onion and green chillies.
Cook until the onion becomes soft.
Add the chopped brinjals and turmeric.
Cook until the brinjals become tender.
Add vangi bath powder and salt.
Mix well and cook for a few minutes.
Add the cooked rice and gently combine.
Cook on low heat so the flavours blend.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve.

name: Karnataka Sambar
description: A flavorful Karnataka-style sambar made with lentils, vegetables, tamarind and aromatic spices.
steps: Wash the toor dal thoroughly.
Cook the dal with turmeric and enough water until soft.
Mash the cooked dal.
Cut the vegetables into small pieces.
Cook the vegetables with chopped tomato until tender.
Soak tamarind and extract the pulp.
Add tamarind pulp, sambar powder and salt to the vegetables.
Simmer until the raw smell of the tamarind disappears.
Add the mashed dal and enough water.
Simmer until the sambar reaches the desired consistency.
Heat oil in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, dried red chillies and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering into the sambar.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Mysore Pak
description: A famous Karnataka sweet made with gram flour, sugar and generous amounts of ghee.
steps: Sieve the gram flour to remove lumps.
Lightly roast the gram flour in a pan.
Prepare a sugar syrup using sugar and water.
Cook the syrup until it reaches a suitable thick consistency.
Gradually add the gram flour while stirring continuously.
Add warm ghee little by little while continuously mixing.
Continue cooking until the mixture becomes thick and starts leaving the sides of the pan.
Grease a suitable tray with ghee.
Transfer the mixture into the tray.
Smooth the surface evenly.
Allow it to cool slightly.
Cut into rectangular or diamond-shaped pieces.
Allow the pieces to cool completely before serving.

name: Karnataka Obbattu
description: A traditional Karnataka sweet flatbread filled with sweetened lentils and flavoured with cardamom.
steps: Wash and cook the chana dal until soft.
Drain excess water completely.
Add jaggery and cook until the mixture becomes thick.
Add cardamom powder and mix well.
Allow the filling to cool and mash it into a smooth mixture.
Prepare a soft dough using maida, water, salt and a little ghee.
Allow the dough to rest.
Divide the dough and filling into equal portions.
Flatten one dough portion and place the filling in the centre.
Seal the edges around the filling.
Gently flatten and roll into a thin circular shape.
Heat a flat pan.
Cook the obbattu with a little ghee on both sides until golden spots appear.
Serve warm.

name: Davangere Benne Dosa
description: A crisp and buttery Karnataka dosa traditionally served with potato palya and chutney.
steps: Wash and soak rice, urad dal and fenugreek separately for several hours.
Soak poha briefly.
Grind the soaked ingredients into a smooth batter.
Mix with salt and allow the batter to ferment.
Prepare a simple potato palya with cooked potatoes, onion and green chillies.
Heat a flat pan.
Pour batter and spread into a dosa.
Add butter around the edges and on top.
Cook until crisp and golden.
Serve hot with potato palya and chutney.

name: Set Dosa
description: Soft, thick and fluffy Karnataka-style dosas usually served in a set of three.
steps: Wash and soak rice, urad dal and fenugreek seeds.
Soak poha separately.
Grind everything into a smooth batter.
Add salt and ferment the batter.
Heat a flat pan over medium heat.
Pour a small ladle of batter without spreading it too thin.
Drizzle a little oil around the dosa.
Cover and cook until the top is set.
Flip briefly if desired.
Serve several dosas together with chutney and sambar.

name: Mangalore Buns
description: Soft, mildly sweet banana puris from coastal Karnataka.
steps: Mash the bananas in a bowl.
Add curd, sugar, cumin, salt and baking soda.
Add maida gradually and form a soft dough.
Cover and rest the dough for several hours.
Divide into small portions.
Roll each portion into a small thick disc.
Heat oil over medium heat.
Fry the buns until puffed and golden.
Drain excess oil.
Serve with coconut chutney or sambar.

name: Mangalore Bajji
description: Soft and fluffy Karnataka-style fritters made with flour, curd and spices.
steps: Combine maida and rice flour.
Add curd, chopped chilli, cumin, curry leaves, baking soda and salt.
Add water and make a thick batter.
Rest the batter for a short time.
Heat oil in a deep pan.
Drop small portions of batter into the oil.
Fry over medium heat until golden and cooked through.
Remove and drain.
Serve hot with chutney.

name: Gojju Avalakki
description: A tangy Karnataka poha preparation made with tamarind, jaggery and spices.
steps: Wash the poha briefly and drain.
Extract tamarind pulp.
Mix tamarind pulp with jaggery, turmeric and salt.
Add the poha and combine gently.
Heat oil in a pan.
Add mustard, cumin, chana dal, peanuts, chillies and curry leaves.
Cook until the tempering is aromatic.
Add the poha mixture.
Mix well and cook briefly.
Serve warm.

name: Kosambari
description: A fresh Karnataka salad made with soaked lentils, cucumber, carrot and coconut.
steps: Wash and soak moong dal for about 30 minutes.
Drain the dal completely.
Finely chop cucumber, carrot and green chilli.
Combine the vegetables, dal and coconut.
Add salt and lemon juice.
Heat a little oil and temper mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over the salad.
Add coriander leaves.
Mix gently and serve fresh.

name: Chitranna
description: Karnataka-style lemon rice with peanuts and a fragrant tempering.
steps: Cool the cooked rice so the grains remain separate.
Heat oil in a pan.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add dals and peanuts and fry until golden.
Add green chillies, dried red chillies and curry leaves.
Add turmeric and turn off the heat.
Squeeze lemon juice into the tempering.
Add the mixture to the rice.
Add salt and mix gently.
Rest briefly before serving.

name: Rava Idli
description: Soft steamed Karnataka semolina idlis flavored with yogurt and a simple tempering.
steps: Dry roast semolina lightly and allow it to cool.
Heat oil and temper mustard seeds, urad dal, cashews and curry leaves.
Add the tempering to semolina.
Add curd, ginger and salt.
Add water to make a thick batter.
Rest briefly.
Add baking soda just before steaming.
Pour into greased idli moulds.
Steam until cooked.
Serve with chutney and sambar.

name: Maddur Vada
description: A crisp Karnataka snack made with rice flour, semolina, onion and spices.
steps: Combine rice flour and semolina.
Add finely chopped onion, chillies, curry leaves, cumin and salt.
Add hot oil and mix carefully.
Add water gradually to make a firm dough.
Take small portions and flatten them into thin discs.
Heat oil over medium heat.
Fry the vadas until crisp and golden.
Drain excess oil.
Serve hot with chutney.

name: Dharwad Peda
description: A traditional Karnataka milk sweet made by reducing milk and sugar to a rich peda mixture.
steps: Pour milk into a heavy pan.
Simmer while stirring regularly until it reduces considerably.
Add milk powder and continue cooking.
Add sugar and cook until the mixture thickens.
Add ghee and cardamom powder.
Continue stirring until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan.
Allow it to cool until easy to handle.
Shape into small pedas.
Serve after cooling completely.

name: Masala Dosa
description: A popular South Indian crisp dosa filled with spiced potato masala.
steps: Soak rice, urad dal and fenugreek seeds.
Grind into a smooth batter and ferment.
Boil and mash the potatoes.
Prepare potato masala with onion, chillies, mustard, curry leaves and turmeric.
Heat a dosa pan.
Spread a thin layer of batter.
Drizzle oil around the edges.
Place potato masala in the centre.
Fold the dosa and cook until crisp.
Serve with chutney and sambar.

name: Karnataka Ragi Rotti
description: A rustic Karnataka flatbread made from ragi flour, onion and green chillies.
steps: Combine ragi flour, chopped onion, chillies, coriander, cumin and salt.
Add water gradually to form a soft dough.
Grease a flat pan.
Spread a portion of dough thinly using wet fingers.
Make a few small holes.
Add oil to the holes and edges.
Cook covered over medium heat.
Cook until the underside is firm.
Serve hot with chutney or curry.

name: Karnataka Vada Curry
description: A spiced curry made with steamed or fried lentil dumplings and aromatic gravy.
steps: Soak chana dal and drain well.
Grind it coarsely with green chillies and salt.
Shape the mixture into small dumplings.
Steam or fry the dumplings until cooked.
Prepare a gravy with oil, onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes.
Add chilli and coriander powder.
Add water and simmer.
Break some dumplings into the gravy and add the remaining whole.
Simmer briefly.
Garnish with coriander.

name: Karnataka Kadubu
description: Steamed Karnataka rice dumplings prepared in sweet or savory styles.
steps: Boil water with a pinch of salt.
Add rice flour gradually and mix.
Cover briefly and allow it to cool enough to handle.
Knead into a soft dough.
Mix coconut, jaggery and cardamom for the filling.
Take a dough portion and flatten it.
Place filling in the centre and seal.
Shape into a dumpling.
Steam until firm and cooked.
Serve warm.

name: Karnataka Saaru
description: A light, tangy and spiced Karnataka lentil-based soup commonly served with rice.
steps: Cook the toor dal until soft and mash it.
Cook chopped tomato with water and turmeric.
Add tamarind pulp and rasam powder.
Add mashed dal and adjust the consistency.
Add salt and simmer.
Heat oil and temper mustard, cumin and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering into the saaru.
Garnish with coriander.
Serve hot with rice.

name: Kerala Appam
description: A lacy Kerala rice pancake with crisp edges and a soft centre.
steps: Soak raw rice for several hours.
Grind rice with cooked rice and coconut milk.
Add yeast, sugar and salt.
Add water to make a pourable batter.
Allow the batter to ferment.
Heat an appam pan.
Pour batter into the centre.
Swirl the pan so the batter spreads around the sides.
Cover and cook until the centre is set and edges are crisp.
Serve with vegetable or coconut-based curry.

name: Puttu
description: Steamed Kerala rice flour cylinders layered with coconut.
steps: Place rice flour in a bowl.
Add salt.
Sprinkle water gradually and mix until the flour becomes moist and crumbly.
Avoid making a smooth dough.
Layer coconut and moistened flour in a puttu mould.
Steam until fully cooked.
Remove carefully from the mould.
Serve with banana, kadala curry or another accompaniment.

name: Kadala Curry
description: A Kerala black chickpea curry flavored with roasted coconut and spices.
steps: Soak chickpeas overnight.
Cook until tender.
Roast coconut with spices until aromatic.
Grind the roasted mixture into a paste.
Heat oil and temper mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Add onion and cook until soft.
Add tomato and cook down.
Add the ground coconut mixture.
Add cooked chickpeas and water.
Simmer until the gravy thickens.
Serve hot with puttu or appam.

name: Avial
description: A Kerala mixed-vegetable preparation cooked with coconut and yogurt.
steps: Cut vegetables into similar-sized pieces.
Cook the vegetables with turmeric, salt and a little water.
Grind coconut, green chillies and cumin into a coarse paste.
Add the coconut paste to the vegetables.
Cook until the vegetables are tender.
Lower the heat and add beaten curd.
Mix gently without boiling strongly.
Add curry leaves and coconut oil.
Serve warm.

name: Kerala Parotta
description: Layered flaky flatbread traditionally served with Kerala curries.
steps: Combine flour, sugar and salt.
Add water and knead into a soft dough.
Add oil and knead until smooth.
Rest the dough covered.
Divide into balls.
Stretch each ball into a thin sheet.
Fold and coil the sheet.
Flatten the coil gently.
Cook on a hot pan with a little oil.
Press and fluff the cooked parotta gently.
Serve with curry.

name: Kerala Fish Curry
description: A tangy Kerala fish curry flavored with tamarind, chilli and coconut oil.
steps: Clean the fish pieces.
Heat coconut oil in a curry pot.
Add ginger, green chillies and curry leaves.
Add chilli, turmeric and coriander powder.
Add water and tamarind or kokum.
Bring the gravy to a simmer.
Add fish pieces carefully.
Cook until the fish is done.
Add coconut milk and heat gently.
Serve with rice.

name: Kerala Beef Fry
description: A Kerala-style spiced beef preparation cooked with onion, ginger, garlic and curry leaves.
steps: Cut the beef into suitable pieces.
Combine beef with spices, ginger-garlic paste and salt.
Cook until tender with a little water.
Heat coconut oil in a wide pan.
Add onions and curry leaves.
Cook until the onions soften.
Add the cooked beef.
Cook uncovered while stirring occasionally.
Add black pepper and garam masala.
Continue until the preparation becomes dry and well coated.
Serve hot.

name: Idiyappam
description: Delicate steamed rice noodles from Kerala, often served with coconut milk or curry.
steps: Boil water with salt and a little oil.
Add hot water gradually to rice flour.
Mix and knead into a soft dough.
Place dough into an idiyappam press.
Press thin strands into greased steaming plates.
Sprinkle grated coconut between layers if desired.
Steam until cooked.
Remove carefully.
Serve with coconut milk or curry.

name: Unniyappam
description: Small Kerala sweet dumplings made with rice, banana, jaggery and coconut.
steps: Mash the banana.
Melt jaggery with a little water and strain.
Combine rice flour, banana, jaggery, coconut, cardamom and sesame seeds.
Add water to make a thick batter.
Rest the batter briefly.
Heat a paniyaram or unniyappam pan with a little ghee.
Fill each cavity with batter.
Cook on low-medium heat.
Turn gently and cook all sides.
Serve warm.

name: Payasam
description: A traditional Kerala-style creamy dessert prepared with milk, rice, sugar and cardamom.
steps: Wash the rice.
Add rice and milk to a heavy pan.
Cook slowly until the rice becomes soft.
Stir regularly to prevent sticking.
Add sugar and continue simmering.
Add cardamom powder.
Fry cashews and raisins in ghee.
Add them to the payasam.
Simmer briefly.
Serve warm or chilled.

name: Pongal
description: A comforting Tamil Nadu rice and moong dal dish seasoned with pepper, cumin and ghee.
steps: Wash rice and moong dal.
Lightly roast the dal if desired.
Cook rice and dal together with enough water until soft.
Mash the mixture lightly.
Heat ghee in a pan.
Add cumin, pepper, ginger, cashews and curry leaves.
Fry until aromatic.
Pour the tempering over the cooked pongal.
Add salt and mix.
Serve hot.

name: Ven Pongal
description: A savory Tamil Nadu pongal with soft rice and dal, black pepper and generous tempering.
steps: Wash rice and dal.
Cook them together with plenty of water until soft.
Mash gently.
Heat ghee.
Add pepper, cumin, ginger, cashews and curry leaves.
Fry until aromatic.
Add the tempering to the rice and dal.
Season with salt.
Mix well.
Serve immediately.

name: Medu Vada
description: Crisp urad dal fritters with a soft centre, commonly served with sambar and chutney.
steps: Soak urad dal for several hours.
Drain thoroughly.
Grind into a thick fluffy batter with very little water.
Add chopped chilli, onion, cumin, curry leaves and salt.
Heat oil in a deep pan.
Shape small portions into rings.
Fry until golden and crisp.
Drain excess oil.
Serve with sambar and chutney.

name: Kanchipuram Idli
description: A spiced Tamil Nadu idli flavored with pepper, cumin, ginger and yogurt.
steps: Soak rice and urad dal separately.
Grind and combine into an idli batter.
Add salt and ferment.
Mix in curd.
Prepare a ghee tempering with pepper, cumin, ginger, cashews and curry leaves.
Add the tempering to the batter.
Pour into greased moulds.
Steam until cooked.
Cool slightly and cut.
Serve with chutney.

name: Kothu Parotta
description: A popular Tamil Nadu street-food dish made by chopping parotta with egg, onion and spices.
steps: Chop the parottas into small pieces.
Heat oil on a wide pan.
Add onion, chillies and curry leaves.
Cook until the onion softens.
Add chopped tomatoes and spices.
Cook until the tomatoes soften.
Push the mixture aside and add beaten eggs.
Scramble the eggs.
Add chopped parotta pieces.
Mix and chop everything together while cooking.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

name: Sambar
description: A classic South Indian lentil and vegetable stew flavored with tamarind and sambar spices.
steps: Wash and cook the toor dal until soft.
Cook chopped vegetables separately or with the dal.
Add tomato, turmeric and sambar powder.
Add tamarind pulp and salt.
Add mashed dal and enough water.
Simmer until the vegetables and dal combine.
Heat oil and temper mustard seeds, dried chillies and curry leaves.
Add the tempering to the sambar.
Simmer briefly.
Serve with rice, idli or dosa.

name: Rasam
description: A light South Indian spiced soup made with tomato, tamarind and rasam spices.
steps: Cook or crush the tomatoes.
Add water and tamarind pulp.
Add rasam powder, cumin, pepper and garlic.
Add salt and bring to a gentle simmer.
Avoid prolonged boiling after the rasam becomes frothy.
Heat oil and temper mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Add the tempering.
Garnish with coriander.
Serve hot with rice or drink as a light soup.

name: Chettinad Chicken
description: A bold Tamil Nadu chicken curry made with roasted spices, coconut and aromatic herbs.
steps: Clean the chicken.
Roast coconut and whole spices until aromatic.
Grind them into a coarse paste.
Heat oil and cook onions until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add powdered spices.
Add chicken and coat with masala.
Add water and cook covered until chicken is done.
Add the roasted spice paste.
Simmer until the gravy thickens.
Garnish and serve.

name: Paruppu Payasam
description: A traditional Tamil sweet made with lentils, jaggery and coconut milk.
steps: Dry roast the moong dal lightly.
Cook until soft.
Melt jaggery with a little water and strain.
Add jaggery to the cooked dal.
Simmer until combined.
Add coconut milk and heat gently.
Add cardamom.
Fry cashews and raisins in ghee.
Add them to the payasam.
Serve warm.

name: Paniyaram
description: Small South Indian rice-and-lentil dumplings cooked in a special paniyaram pan.
steps: Prepare or use fermented dosa batter.
Heat oil and temper mustard seeds and urad dal.
Add onion, chilli and curry leaves.
Cook until the onion softens.
Mix the tempering into the batter.
Heat a paniyaram pan and grease the cavities.
Pour batter into each cavity.
Cook on low-medium heat.
Turn each paniyaram carefully.
Cook until golden on all sides.
Serve with chutney.

name: Poha
description: A popular Maharashtra breakfast made with flattened rice, peanuts, onion and mild spices.
steps: Rinse the poha and drain well.
Heat oil in a pan.
Add mustard, cumin and peanuts.
Add chillies, curry leaves and onion.
Cook until the onion softens.
Add turmeric and salt.
Add the drained poha.
Mix gently and cook for a few minutes.
Turn off the heat and add lemon juice.
Garnish with coriander and serve.

name: Misal Pav
description: A spicy Maharashtra street-food dish of sprouted beans topped with farsan and served with pav.
steps: Cook the sprouts until tender.
Heat oil and cook chopped onion.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add turmeric, chilli powder and misal masala.
Add cooked sprouts and water.
Simmer until the usal develops flavor.
Adjust salt and consistency.
Serve in bowls topped with farsan and coriander.
Serve with pav, onion and lemon.

name: Pav Bhaji
description: A Mumbai-style street food made from mashed vegetables cooked with bhaji masala and served with buttered pav.
steps: Boil potatoes, cauliflower and peas until soft.
Mash the cooked vegetables.
Heat butter and cook onion.
Add capsicum and tomatoes.
Add pav bhaji masala and chilli powder.
Add mashed vegetables.
Add water and mash while simmering.
Cook until thick and well combined.
Toast pav with butter.
Garnish bhaji with coriander and serve with pav.

name: Puran Poli
description: A traditional Maharashtra sweet flatbread stuffed with sweetened chana dal and jaggery.
steps: Cook chana dal until soft and drain excess water.
Cook dal with jaggery until thick.
Add cardamom and nutmeg.
Mash or grind the filling smoothly.
Prepare a soft wheat flour dough with salt and water.
Rest the dough.
Divide dough and filling into portions.
Stuff each dough portion with filling.
Seal and flatten gently.
Roll into a thin circle.
Cook on a hot pan with ghee.
Serve warm.

name: Modak
description: A steamed Indian sweet dumpling filled with coconut and jaggery.
steps: Heat jaggery with a little water.
Add grated coconut and cook until the mixture thickens.
Add cardamom and set the filling aside.
Boil water with a pinch of salt and a little ghee.
Add rice flour gradually and mix.
Cover briefly and knead into a soft dough.
Take small dough portions and flatten them.
Place coconut-jaggery filling in the centre.
Shape the dough into a closed dumpling.
Steam the modaks until the outer layer becomes firm and cooked.
Serve warm.
